source.title: Spinning Up
source.scope: States and Observations only; initial content pilot, not the entire introduction.

questions.prompt: In reinforcement learning, how does an observation differ from the environment state?
questions.answer: The state describes the world completely. An observation can leave out some of that information.

questions.prompt: In deep reinforcement learning, which numerical structures commonly represent states and observations?
questions.answer: Real-valued vectors, matrices, or tensors of higher order.

questions.prompt: In reinforcement learning, what information can represent a visual observation or a robot state?
questions.answer: An image observation can use RGB pixel values; a robot state can use joint positions and velocities.

questions.prompt: In reinforcement learning, what distinguishes full from partial observability?
questions.answer: Full observability gives the agent the complete environment state. Partial observability exposes only part of it.

questions.prompt: In reinforcement learning notation, why can an action appear conditioned on state $s$ even when the agent only receives observation $o$?
questions.answer: Authors often use $s$ by convention while the implemented decision actually depends on $o$. Read the notation in context.
